extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners before the USPTO; USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, procedural requirements, and sanctions applicable to registered patent practitioners in USPTO disciplinary proceedings (findings of misconduct, suspension, probation, reinstatement, publication, restitution). Includes the OED Director and USPTO Director's processes under 35 U.S.C. and 37 C.F.R.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of Disciplinary Rules / Jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is subject to the Disciplinary Rules of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility (Part 10 of Title 37, CFR). The USPTO Director has jurisdiction under 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes that registered patent agents and attorneys are governed by Part 10 (37 C.F.R.) and that disciplinary proceedings are within USPTO Director/OED jurisdiction per cited statutes and regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neglect of entrusted legal matters (37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct violating 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c) includes allowing clients' patent applications to become abandoned without clients' consent and failing to adequately supervise delegated matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The stipulated facts show abandonment due to missed notices/fees and inadequate supervision; such conduct supports a finding of neglect under §10.77(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to supervise staff when delegating client matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must adequately supervise office staff to whom important client matters are delegated; failure to do so can constitute disciplineable neglect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegation is permissible but practitioner remains responsible; staffing or clerical problems are not an absolute defense where inadequate supervision contributed to client harm (abandonment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension as sanction (terms and commencement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall be suspended from practicing before the Office for twenty-four (24) months commencing on the date the Final Order is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension may be conditioned (see limited recognition and probation). The order specifies exact duration and start date tied to the Final Order signature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition for narrow purpose (30 days to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is granted limited recognition to practice before the Office commencing on the date this Final Order is signed and expiring thirty (30) days thereafter, solely to facilitate compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited recognition is narrowly confined in time and purpose (to effectuate compliance with a specific regulation) and does not negate the overall suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58 and 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58, and the OED Director shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order explicitly imposes compliance obligations on both the respondent and OED; these CFR sections govern suspension/reinstatement procedures and OED's duties when reinstatement is sought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for reinstatement timing and procedure (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: At any time after twelve (12) months from the date the Final Order is signed, Respondent may file a petition for reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 requesting reinstatement effective prior to the expiration of the 24-month suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement is governed by §11.60; filing earlier than 12 months is not permitted, and rehearing/reinstatement procedures follow the cited regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension remains until OED Director grants reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall remain suspended from practice before the Office until the OED Director grants a petition requesting Respondent's reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if time has passed, status is controlled by OED's action granting reinstatement under the regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation requirement (24 months)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall serve a twenty-four (24) month period of probation beginning on the date this Final Order is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Probation runs concurrently with the order and carries monitoring/enforcement consequences for noncompliance (see Order to Show Cause provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Order to Show Cause process for probation violations
rubrics_metrics.description: If OED Director believes Respondent failed to comply with the Final Order or any Disciplinary Rule during probation, OED Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause and: (A) if not yet reinstated, seek an order barring Respondent from filing a request for reinstatement during the 24-month suspension; or (B) if reinstated, seek immediate suspension up to an additional twelve (12) months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural requirements include sending the Order to Show Cause to Respondent's last address of record, granting 15 days to respond, and following a two-step submission to the USPTO Director with Respondent's response and OED's supporting argument/evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and response timeframe for Order to Show Cause
rubrics_metrics.description: OED Director shall send the Order to Show Cause to Respondent at the last address of record and grant Respondent fifteen (15) days to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fifteen days is the specific short response window; OED must consider the response before deciding further action or forwarding to the USPTO Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral to USPTO Director and available relief
rubrics_metrics.description: After consideration of Respondent's response (if any), OED Director may deliver the Order to Show Cause, Respondent's response, and argument/evidence to the USPTO Director, requesting either (i) a bar on filing a reinstatement request during the 24-month suspension, or (ii) an immediate additional suspension up to twelve months if Respondent was reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes the escalation path and remedies available to the USPTO Director once OED forwards the matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative consequences upon additional discipline (dissociation of electronic credentials)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the USPTO Director enters an order barring Respondent from filing a request for reinstatement or immediately suspends Respondent further, the USPTO shall promptly dissociate Respondent's name from all USPTO Customer Numbers and Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) certificates, and Respondent may not apply for or obtain a USPTO Customer Number unless and until reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative access (customer numbers/PKI) is revoked as part of enforcement to prevent practice before the Office while barred/suspended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of review on operation of the Director's order
rubrics_metrics.description: If Respondent seeks review of the USPTO Director's action under subparagraph g, any such review shall not operate to postpone or otherwise hold in abeyance the USPTO Director's order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Challenges to Director orders do not stay the order; the discipline remains in effect during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order (OED Reading Room and Official Gazette)
rubrics_metrics.description: OED Director shall publish this Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room (names and application numbers may be redacted) and shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided notice of suspension and probation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public notice is required; redaction of client names/application numbers is permitted. The Official Gazette notice includes succinct facts and sanctions (suspension length, eligibility to request reinstatement after 12 months, probation, restitution info).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restitution payment obligations and schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall pay restitution of $810.00 in strict compliance with the schedule: (i) $405.00 as soon thereafter as practical given the signature date, and (ii) $405.00 on or before March 1, 2012.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payments must follow the precise schedule set forth in the order; amounts and due dates are mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of restitution payments (affidavit and corroborating documents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within fifteen (15) days of the due date of each payment, Respondent shall provide the OED Director with an affidavit and corroborating documents (e.g., copy of the payment letter mailed to the client) demonstrating compliance with payment obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely documentary proof to OED is required; absence of proof may trigger enforcement actions under the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED motion to dismiss pending proceeding upon compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Within thirty (30) days of the date this Final Order is signed, the OED Director shall file a motion to dismiss the disciplinary proceeding currently pending against Respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing to dismiss is conditioned on settlement/agreement; the order sets a 30-day deadline for the motion to be filed by OED.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reservation of right to seek further discipline (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.34–11.57)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement or Final Order prevents the Office from seeking discipline against Respondent under 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.34 through 11.57 for the misconduct that caused the Director to enter an order barring reinstatement or immediately suspending Respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The settlement does not preclude later separate disciplinary proceedings or additional penalties under the specified CFR provisions if further or related misconduct occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of this record in future proceedings (aggravating/rebuttal factor)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may consider the record of this disciplinary proceeding, including this Final Order, in any future complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct (i) as an aggravating factor in determining discipline and/or (ii) to rebut any statement or representation by Respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior discipline and the written Final Order can be used to aggravate sanctions or to counter claims in subsequent disciplinary matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs between parties
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement allocates no cross-party cost award; each party pays its own costs related to the proceeding and implementing the agreement.
